# FreeModel

29 models (Claude, GPT, DeepSeek, Kimi and more) behind one OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

| | |
|---|---|
| Kind | Chat API (OpenAI-compatible): returns code that conductor-ai applies |
| Cost | 1M tokens a month, no card; requests stop with HTTP 402 when they run out. |
| Key | `FREEMODEL_API_KEY` from https://freemodel.in/register (the provider's docs name no variable; this is conductor-ai's name for it) |
| Endpoint | `https://freemodel.in/v1` |
| Default model | picked automatically from the live list (coding models first); choose your own with `conductor-ai models freemodel --all` |
| conductor-ai name | `freemodel` |
| Privacy | Says it does not store prompts or replies, but they go to the upstream model provider, whose retention applies. |
| Provider docs | https://freemodel.in/docs/getting-started |
| Checked | 2026-11 |

## Set up

1. Create an API key: https://freemodel.in/register
2. Add it to conductor-ai. It asks for the key (hidden input), lets you pick a model, sends one test prompt and adds it to the `docs`, `test`, `review` and `ask` roles:
   ```bash
   conductor-ai add freemodel
   ```
3. Check it any time:
   ```bash
   conductor-ai doctor --live
   ```

Or click **Add** on its card in `conductor-ai ui` → Providers.

## Without the wizard

Save the key (hidden input; or pipe it in):
```bash
conductor-ai keys set FREEMODEL_API_KEY
```

Then add this to `~/.config/conductor-ai/config.json` (all projects) or `.conductor-ai/config.json` (one project):
```json
{
  "providers": {
    "freemodel": {
      "type": "openai",
      "enabled": true,
      "baseUrl": "https://freemodel.in/v1",
      "apiKeyEnv": "FREEMODEL_API_KEY",
      "model": "<model id>"
    }
  }
}
```
List models: `conductor-ai models freemodel --all`. Put `freemodel` in any role's chain in `conductor-ai ui` → Roles & fallback.

The variable name only tells conductor-ai where to find the key; the provider never sees it. To use a key you already keep under another name, set `"apiKeyEnv": "YOUR_VAR"` on `freemodel`.

## Troubleshooting

- **401 / 403**: the key is wrong, expired, or still a placeholder. Run `conductor-ai keys` to see where it comes from, then `conductor-ai keys set FREEMODEL_API_KEY`.
- **404 or "model not found"**: the model id changed. Pick a current one with `conductor-ai models freemodel --all`.
- **429**: rate limit. conductor-ai puts the provider on cooldown and moves to the next one in the chain; `conductor-ai cooldown --clear freemodel` resets it.
- **Empty reply**: some free routes return nothing now and then; conductor-ai retries once, then falls back.
